instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: Assistant Chat is a presentation consumer of provider, account, model, effort, and route-specific media capability schemas. It must expose requested/effective and unsupported or fallback outcomes without deriving truth from legacy platform tables.
atoms.title: Chat consumes rather than owns provider and media capability truth

atoms.statement: Thread-bound operations use repo, worktree, and relative-path identity, and turn start freezes worktree and working-directory context. Historical evidence remains pinned when later rebinding occurs.
atoms.title: Worktree identity is frozen per turn and path alone is non-canonical

atoms.statement: Creation spans a worktree record, thread binding, reverse lookup, and seglog event, but the unit defines atomicity only for one reverse-lookup write. It does not specify transaction ordering, rollback, or authoritative reconciliation after a crash between writes.
atoms.title: Binding persistence has no atomic commit or reconciliation contract

atoms.statement: The GUI specifies accessible labels and polite announcements for lifecycle changes, and it distinguishes stale last-known status from fresh status rather than presenting it as current.
atoms.title: Worktree status includes accessibility and stale-projection disclosure

atoms.statement: The cleanup contract says delete, unbind, prune, and emit an event, but it does not define which state commits first or what the UI and stores retain if force removal or branch deletion fails after thread deletion.
atoms.title: Thread deletion and destructive worktree removal lack failure ordering

atoms.statement: The merge lock is removed when older than five minutes even if the recorded process is still alive, while the permitted pre-merge test timeout reaches thirty minutes. No heartbeat, owner-instance token, or live-process age exception prevents two merge sequences from overlapping.
atoms.title: Five-minute stale-lock rule can unlock a legitimate long merge

atoms.statement: Execution checks main-repo dirtiness only for squash or merge with merged-result testing, yet all no-test strategies and branch-only paths can later checkout the target in the main working tree. The contract does not say how unrelated dirty files are preserved or why those paths are safe.
atoms.title: Main-repository dirty guard does not cover every checkout path

atoms.statement: Push and API failures are phase-distinguished and do not open the PR panel. A successful push followed by API failure intentionally leaves the remote branch side effect and the local worktree binding in place.
atoms.title: PR failures preserve the pushed branch and keep the worktree bound

atoms.statement: The merged-result rebase flow completes git rebase before running tests, then prescribes git rebase --abort on test failure. After a successful rebase completes there is normally no active rebase operation to abort, so the promised clean rollback is not implementable as written.
atoms.title: Post-rebase test failure cannot be recovered with rebase abort

atoms.statement: Merge is disabled while the project merge lock is held, but PR is enabled without a lock condition and performs a branch push. The assigned unit does not define serialization between push, rebase, merge, rename, or branch deletion.
atoms.title: PR push can race merge because enablement omits the merge lock

atoms.statement: Worktree, file, terminal, provider CLI, and chat operations remain remote-host-scoped. Offline and stale states must be disclosed, and missing remote CLIs cannot trigger silent local execution or installation.
atoms.title: Remote projects preserve remote host authority with no silent local fallback

atoms.statement: The text correctly forbids approval leakage across lanes, accounts, and actors, but only demands a canonical actor/account/lane scope key; it does not provide the key fields, normalization rules, lifetime, or invalidation events.
atoms.title: Permission approval scope key is required but not defined

atoms.statement: The unit says retry memory and handoff are structured records, then states that the design still must choose JSONL versus redb ownership, concrete path or delivery domain, and bounded-packet delivery. Those are build-blocking contracts, not builder discretion.
atoms.title: Worker handoff persistence and delivery remain explicitly unresolved

atoms.statement: ACD-001 is retained solely for migration lineage and cannot re-own atomized product coverage. ACD-002 owns the shared chat UX and source-authority anchors while preserving original prose for exact audit.
atoms.title: Retired bridge lineage is separated from live assistant-chat authority

atoms.statement: The blocked packet names both allowed_action_ids[] and allowed_action_ids but does not distinguish schema notation from separate fields or define normalization. Ordering is required, so ambiguous decoding can change the recovery action shown.
atoms.title: Blocked-notice action field has two spellings without normalization

atoms.statement: The rewrite chat surface must display requested and effective runtime identity while consuming the existing provider and auth field set. Gemini Direct, Antigravity, and retired Gemini CLI lineage may not collapse into one generic badge.
atoms.title: Requested and effective provider identity remains concrete

atoms.statement: The UI closes workflow identity to Ask, Agent, Debug, Plan, and Deep Plan while saying only runtime posture normalizes to the run-envelope mode. No table maps every workflow and approval state to legal regular, yolo, or plan envelopes, including resumed and failed flows.
atoms.title: Workflow-to-run-envelope normalization lacks a complete mapping

atoms.statement: Planning runs are read-only with respect to project files. Approved execution must start under regular or yolo and reuse the approved plan or TODO state; queueing cannot convert the planning run itself into execution.
atoms.title: Plan and Deep Plan cannot mutate project files before approval

atoms.statement: Debug is an execution-capable overlay with named phases and mandatory drift revalidation, but the unit supplies no closed enum, transition guards, drift detector inputs, evidence record shape, retry path, or cleanup failure recovery.
atoms.title: Debug revalidation phases lack executable transition and evidence schemas

atoms.statement: Platform, model, effort, and worktree controls are visible in the header, sourced from account-bound registries and capability resolution, and apply only to the next turn while an in-flight response retains its frozen choice.
atoms.title: Header selection changes are next-turn state

atoms.statement: Chat ELI5 affects assistant behavior only; app-level ELI5 affects authored tooltips and interviewer answers. Neither changes generated technical documentation.
atoms.title: Chat and app ELI5 controls have independent scope

atoms.statement: Regular mode exposes deny, once, session, and always approval choices, while durable approval defaults remain owned by Permissions System rather than Chat.
atoms.title: Regular permission posture delegates durable defaults to Permissions System

atoms.statement: The unit fixes FIFO capacity at two and scopes Stop, Edit, and Resend to the latest user message, but does not define the third-send result, whether queued messages count as later history, how edit or resend transforms them, or what confirmation protects discarded work.
atoms.title: Message rewrite and bounded queue interactions are under-specified

atoms.statement: The footer combines send/stop, queue affordance, latest-message actions, and compact files-touched rows synchronized with operation cards; transient queue text does not restore after reload.
atoms.title: Footer files-touched display is a projection, not a second status model

atoms.statement: Reserved commands remain canonical and non-overridable. Retired aliases are compatibility lineage and cannot suppress active dispatch.
atoms.title: Built-in commands cannot be overridden by retired aliases or user commands

atoms.statement: ACD-015 promises URL normalization and capability disclosure but, within the complete assigned unit, defines no scheme allowlist, localhost or private-network policy, redirect bound, response-size limit, download handling, or credential-forwarding rule.
atoms.title: Web URL normalization has no untrusted-network safety contract

atoms.statement: The GUI panel, slash command, and natural language all converge on invoke_skill. Bare /skill lists skills, and the MVP does not create a second subcommand dispatcher.
atoms.title: Skill discovery routes converge on one invocation path

atoms.statement: Local repository requests stay in source-control commands, hosted requests stay in GitHub commands, and cross-domain handoffs preserve repo, worktree, and compare identity. User commands may complement but never replace PM-native built-ins.
atoms.title: Git, GitHub, and custom-command authority boundaries are explicit

atoms.statement: Slash, palette, natural language, assistant, subagent, Goal Runtime, PRD Builder, and Planning Wizard calls use one dispatcher. Site or page reading resolves to webfetch rather than websearch.
atoms.title: All web intent callers share dispatch and reading is not search

atoms.statement: Teach is a capture workflow, not a mode. Storage requires explicit user confirmation, and each record declares thread, project, or user scope with identity, provenance, capture, supersession, and revocation metadata.
atoms.title: Teach requires confirmation and explicit durable scope

atoms.statement: The unit prohibits persisting credentials and exposes revocation, but does not specify secret classification, redaction before logging, false-positive handling, encryption, retention, physical deletion, backup propagation, or proof that revoked content no longer enters prompts.
atoms.title: Teach secret exclusion lacks detection and erasure oracles

atoms.statement: Thread, project, and user scopes plus supersession are named, but no deterministic precedence rule covers simultaneous records, divergent multi-window updates, cross-scope contradictions, or revoked records referenced by a newer record.
atoms.title: Teach scope precedence and concurrent conflict resolution are unknown

atoms.statement: Attachments preserve provenance and minimum display fields, but the assigned units define no content hash, size ceiling, storage authority, retention and deletion behavior, missing-source state, malware or active-content handling, upload cancellation, or offline retry semantics.
atoms.title: Attachment schema omits storage, safety, and lifecycle limits

atoms.statement: Voice input becomes visible draft text, browser captures remain visible and removable chips, and selection or element-pick commands never auto-send or inject hidden context.
atoms.title: Browser and voice capture remain visible drafts until send

atoms.statement: A related turn must show web activity and source or citation disclosure, preserve fetched material separately from synthesis, and disclose provider or policy inability rather than implying web access succeeded.
atoms.title: Web use must expose activity, provenance, and inability

atoms.statement: The canonical lifecycle is written as draft to incomplete to ready_to_submit to submitted to paused, while dismissal elsewhere pauses before submission. No transition table says from which states pause is legal, whether submitted is terminal, or which prior state resume restores.
atoms.title: Question lifecycle order is not a valid transition graph

atoms.statement: single_question promotes into a one-item questionnaire envelope, legacy aliases normalize to canonical answer arrays and option objects, and allow_freeform replaces retired allow_other.
atoms.title: Legacy question shapes normalize before storage and validation

atoms.statement: The rendering unit specifies checkbox layout, styling parity, and source context but no keyboard traversal, focus restoration, screen-reader group labeling, validation announcement, text expansion, bidirectional layout, or stable option-ID behavior across localized labels.
atoms.title: Question cards lack interaction accessibility and localization oracles

atoms.statement: ACD-030 makes dismissal a canonical pause path and preserves /dismiss, then lists /dismiss as stale_retired_terms. It does not say whether only the slash command is retired, what command replaces it, or whether dismissal remains reachable only through GUI close.
atoms.title: Dismiss is behaviorally active but marked stale or retired

atoms.statement: Subagents escalate questions to the parent orchestrator unless explicitly re-enabled by run configuration. Headless or unavailable HITL surfaces return unavailable rather than fabricating answers.
atoms.title: Subagents are default-denied from direct user questioning

atoms.statement: Both modes project to one locked TODO model and a checklist-forward review surface with structural editing before approval and live progress tied to the same projection.
atoms.title: Plan and Deep Plan share visible normalized TODO review

atoms.statement: ACD-034 requires revisions, diff resynchronization, durable update events, and explicit replans, but does not define optimistic concurrency, revision preconditions, event ordering, or a gate preventing execution from starting against a TODO projection still being resynced.
atoms.title: Artifact edit, TODO revision, approval, and run start lack one transaction boundary

atoms.statement: Plan and Deep Plan expose Light, Balanced, and Comprehensive, default to Balanced, and use the selection to control question, local-research, web-research, risk, alternative, dependency, validation, and TODO detail.
atoms.title: Plan Thoroughness is a visible three-level intensity control

atoms.statement: The matrix fixes numeric ceilings and source preference but does not define what consumes a question or research unit, whether parallel calls count individually, whether retries consume budget, how unused budget is surfaced, or what happens when the ceiling is reached with unresolved critical uncertainty.
atoms.title: Thoroughness ceilings lack counting and exhaustion semantics

atoms.statement: Standard Plan targets medium-complexity work, expects clarification, prefers repository research, and remains read-only. Its written plan and normalized TODO appear in the plan panel; editor opening is available but not automatic.
atoms.title: Standard Plan is read-only and its artifact opens only on demand

atoms.statement: Deep Plan uses more questions and broader local and web research than Standard Plan at the same PT. It emits a rich markdown document and automatically opens a preview-capable editor surface.
atoms.title: Deep Plan differs by intensity and automatically opens its artifact

atoms.statement: ACD-041 names generated:// buffers as transient but does not define lifetime, crash or restart behavior, save-as transition, ownership, concurrent edits, close warning, garbage collection, or how TODO projections behave if the buffer disappears.
atoms.title: Transient generated artifacts have no persistence or crash lifecycle

atoms.statement: The source declares Markdown and Mermaid canonical and richly rendered but provides no sanitization profile, script or link policy, external resource policy, diagram complexity limit, timeout, or fallback for malicious or pathological generated content.
atoms.title: Rich Markdown and Mermaid preview lacks an untrusted-rendering boundary

atoms.statement: Every Deep Plan document must include the minimum sections, while optional sections remain permitted without becoming universal requirements.
atoms.title: Deep Plan document minimums are explicit and testable

atoms.statement: TODO items use order_index and notes, legacy payloads normalize into the assistant schema, and superseded TODO counts remain plan-level summaries rather than an active item status.
atoms.title: Normalized TODO schema owns canonical fields and legacy conversion

atoms.statement: The primary mode strip is explicitly closed to Ask, Agent, Debug, Plan, and Deep Plan, with specialized workflows normalized as overlays rather than replacements.
atoms.title: Primary Assistant mode vocabulary is closed

atoms.statement: Debug Mode defines a closed phase model with mandatory revalidation before drifted mutation and a falsifiable resolution oracle requiring verification.
atoms.title: Debug resolution is gated by revalidation and verification

atoms.statement: The Stop contract names `chat_run.cancel_timeout` but does not define whether the queue advances after timeout, how late lease results are quarantined, or what recovery state owns still-running model, tool, or subagent work.
atoms.title: Cancel timeout lacks late-effect containment

atoms.statement: The phrase `per-session or per-chat` leaves the persistence owner and precedence of execution mode unresolved, especially when chat state, app settings, and durable approval defaults disagree.
atoms.title: Execution-mode persistence scope is unresolved

atoms.statement: Teach defines explicit persistence scopes and prohibits credential storage, while user-level persistence is conditioned on content not being project-confidential.
atoms.title: Teach persistence has explicit scope and secret boundaries

atoms.statement: Browser capture is explicitly represented as visible pending chips with separate selection and element types and no auto-send behavior.
atoms.title: Browser capture remains visible and user-controlled

atoms.statement: The prose lifecycle orders `submitted → paused` while simultaneously saying pause occurs on dismissal without submission, and the canonical envelope adds separate `dismissed`, `timed_out`, and `unavailable` flow states without transitions.
atoms.title: Questionnaire lifecycle contradicts its canonical enum

atoms.statement: The PT matrix gives numeric question ceilings but leaves research breadth and web activation to phrases such as `when helpful`, without observable trigger thresholds or minimum work needed to distinguish adjacent PT levels.
atoms.title: Plan Thoroughness research triggers are subjective

atoms.statement: The normalized TODO contract owns item ordering, notes, status semantics, and legacy tool-payload normalization without minting a second checklist schema.
atoms.title: TODO projection has a single normalized contract

atoms.statement: Annotation revision recovery preserves revision lineage and validated outcomes rather than replaying the entire run without identity.
atoms.title: Targeted revision recovery preserves safe-point lineage

atoms.statement: The planning-to-execution handoff has a direct oracle: explicit approval is mandatory and the follow-on runtime posture must be regular or explicitly selected yolo, never plan.
atoms.title: Plan execution requires explicit approval

atoms.statement: Auto-retrieval requires deterministic per-source query, hit, and byte caps but supplies no values, derivation rule, configuration owner, or observable cap-hit behavior beyond truncation notes.
atoms.title: Auto-retrieval budget caps have no values

atoms.statement: The lifecycle contract says active threads keep queue state while restore explicitly excludes ephemeral queue state, but it does not distinguish durable queue metadata from transient queued content or define the suspension transition cleanup.
atoms.title: Thread restore leaves queue persistence boundary unclear

atoms.statement: The final-state mapping emits `failed`, but reopen semantics enumerate only resolved, cancelled, and superseded terminal histories and provide no failed-state lifecycle or recovery rule.
atoms.title: Failed investigation state has no lifecycle semantics

atoms.statement: Reopen semantics require `attention_required_reason_code`, while the canonical Investigation Context header imports `attention_reason_code?`; no alias or migration rule reconciles them.
atoms.title: Attention reason field names conflict

atoms.statement: The Raw pane promises full serialized payloads but does not define viewer authorization, field-level secret scrubbing, reveal consent, export behavior, or retention limits; displaying redaction state does not itself specify what must be redacted.
atoms.title: Raw Context Detail lacks an access and scrubbing contract

atoms.statement: The operation-card family has an explicit ownership and exclusion boundary for command, web/search, and diff/edit lifecycle artifacts.
atoms.title: Operation-card exclusions prevent widget-family conflation

atoms.statement: The canonical text leaves Firecrawl `changeTracking` as an either-preserve-or-retire branch instead of deciding the product capability and migration outcome.
atoms.title: Firecrawl change tracking remains an open product branch

atoms.statement: The batch permission rule grants all listed domains after one prompt but does not define deselection, partial approval, denial of one domain, grant revocation, or how the batch proceeds when only a subset is authorized.
atoms.title: Batch domain approval has no partial-grant semantics

atoms.statement: The early chip vocabulary uses waiting and done while the canonical table later uses awaiting_parent, blocked, complete, cancelled, and queued.

atoms.statement: Context Lens lacks a run-snapshot boundary, concurrent-edit ordering, and explicit rollback semantics for already-created Subcompact summaries.

atoms.statement: The implementation has fixed defaults but no measurable performance acceptance oracle for tuning or release gating.

atoms.title: Host-readiness cards preserve mutation ownership

atoms.statement: ACD-430 names only a future feature fixture in addition to structural plan-index validation, leaving runtime GUI behavior uncertified.
atoms.title: ACD-430 lacks a current executable behavior oracle

atoms.statement: Deep Plan performs a final wizard-escalation evaluation before defaulting to chat execution and recommends Planning Wizard when work spans several domains, has unresolved material questions, reads like a feature spec, or should produce orchestrator-ready artifacts.
atoms.title: Deep Planning Wizard Escalation Evaluation

atoms.statement: The bundle field list has no types, required/optional rules, schema version, size bounds, redaction policy, authorization check, idempotency key, or partial-launch recovery.
atoms.title: Wizard handoff schema lacks versioning, bounds, and redaction

atoms.statement: The pointer fields include redaction state but do not define access checks at dereference time, retention and deletion semantics, stale or moved message recovery, range bounds, or audit logging.
atoms.title: Excerpt dereference authorization and stale-reference behavior are missing

atoms.statement: The unit does not specify where imported context appears, how users inspect source lineage and redaction, what audit event fields persist, or how hidden/immediate-execution violations are tested.
atoms.title: Visible and auditable handoff states lack concrete oracles

atoms.statement: Project/path 'exists' is not tied to an authority or validation rule, and missing permissions, stale paths, launch failure, duplicate accept, and return-to-chat recovery are unspecified.
atoms.title: Wizard launch context routing has no validation or rollback path
